q: The distance between the end projectors of a line PQ is 60 mm. The point P is 20mm below HP and 25mm behind VP. Point Q is 12mm above HP and 40mm in front of VP. Draw projections of line PQ. Also find its true length and its inclinations with HP and VP.
Differentiate between First Angle and Third Angle projection methods.

A line PQ is 120 mm long. It is inclined at 45° to the HP and 30° to the VP. The end P is 15 mm above HP and 25 mm in front of VP. Assuming the end Q in the first quadrant, draw the projections of the line PQ.
Fig. 1 shows pictorial view of an object. Draw following views: (1) Front view looking in the direction X, (2) Left Hand Side View. Use first angle projection method.

The major and minor Axis of an ellipse is 120 mm and 80 mm respectively. Draw upper half ellipse by concentric circle method and lower half by arc of circle method. Also Find distance between its foci points.

A pentagonal pyramid side of base 30 mm and 60 mm height rests with its base on HP. One of the edges of its base is perpendicular to VP. A section plane perpendicular to VP and inclined at 45° to HP bisects the axis. Draw the sectional top view and front view. Also draw the true shape of the section.
Explain different types of lines with their illustrations and applications.
Write three advantages of AutoCAD over conventional manual drawing.
The foci of an ellipse are 120mm apart. The minor axis 72 mm long. Determine the length of the major axis and draw ellipse by oblong method.
Construct the involute of circle of 30mm diameter for one turn.
Differentiate between prism and pyramid
A line PQ 70 mm long has its end P in VP and end Q in HP. Line is inclined to HP by 600 and VP by 300. Draw the projections
Define Cycloid. Also explain in brief about its types using suitable sketch.
Draw a diagonal scale of R.F, 1:12 showing yard, feet and inch and long enough to measure up to 3 yards. Show a distance of 1 yard 2 feet and 3 inch on it.
A semicircular plate of 90mm diameter has its straight edge in the HP and inclined at 45⁰ to the VP. The surface of the plate makes an angle of 30⁰ with the HP. Draw its projections.
A line CD is 70mm long. Point C is 20mm above HP and 30 mm in front of VP and point D is 60mm above HP and 50 mm in front of VP. Draw its projections.
Explain difference between orthographic projection and isometric projection.

Draw projections of the following points along a same reference line keeping 25 mm distance between projectors. (i) A in the HP, 20 behind VP. (ii) B 40 above HP, 25 in front of VP. (iii) C in the VP, 40 above HP
Classify ‘solids’ in detail.
Differentiate between ‘polyhedra’ and ‘solids of revolution’.

A circular disc of diameter AB = 90 mm, rotates with uniform angular velocity. The point P which is at A, moves with uniform linear velocity and reaches the point B, when the disc completes one revolution. Trace the locus of point P moving from A to B.

Construct an ellipse when the distance of its focus from its directrix is equal to 50 mm and the eccentricity is 2/3. Also, draw the tangent and normal to the ellipse at a point 70 mm away from the directrix.
Define ellipse, parabola and hyperbola based on eccentricity ratio.
What are the advantages and disadvantages of using AUTOCAD?
Differentiate between aligned system and unidirectional system of dimensioning using sketches.
Draw isometric scale showing 100 mm normal scale.
Explain the following AUTOCAD commands (i) Trim, (ii) Arc, (iii) Mirror, (iv) Array
Fig. 2 shows F.V. and T.V. of an object. Draw isometric view.
Draw the projections of a 100 mm long line PQ which is inclined at an angle of 45° to H.P. and 30° to V.P. One of its end point ‘P’ is in H.P. as well as in VP.

ABCD is a rhombus of diagonals AC = 110 mm and BD =70 mm. Its corner A is in the H.P. and the plane is inclined to H.P. such that the plan appears to be a square. The plan of diagonal AC makes an angle of 20o to the V.P. Draw the projections of the plane and find its inclination with H.P. (Hint. Take a scale of 1:2)
A circular plate of diameter 50 mm is resting on H.P. on a point on the circumference with its surface inclined at 45° to H.P. and perpendicular to V.P. Draw its projections.

A cone, base diameter 80 mm and axis length 80 mm is resting on its base on the H.P. It is cut by an AIP inclined at 45o to the H.P. and cutting the axis at 30 mm from the apex. Draw front view, sectional top view and true shape of the section.

Draw the projection of following points on the same X-Y line. (1) Point A is 25 mm above HP and 30 mm behind V.P. (2) Point B is 20 mm above HP and on V.P. (3) Point C is 10 mm bellow HP and 25 mm behind V.P. (4) Point D is on HP and 40 mm in front of V.P.

A square pyramid, base 40 mm side and axis 65 mm long, has its base on the HP and all the edges of the base equally inclined to the VP. It is cut by a section plane, perpendicular to the VP, inclined at 45º to the HP and bisecting the axis. Draw its development.
An isosceles triangular XYZ having its base XY=50 and altitude 60mm is resting on H.P. on is base XY with its surface making and angle of 450 to H.P. Draw projection of plane.
Draw regular pentagon and hexagon of 30 mm side using UNIVERSAL METHOD
Draw following projection of points: (1) Point ‘A’ is 25 mm above HP and 20 mm Infront of VP. (2) Point ‘B’ is 35 mm behind VP and 40 mm above HP. (3) Point ‘C’ is in the HP and 10 mm Infront of VP
Draw projections of line AB=85 mm inclined to 60° HP & 30° VP

A pentagonal plate, side 25 mm is resting on H.P. on one of its corners with opposite edge to the corner making 30° with V.P. The plate is inclined to H.P. by 45°. Draw the projections of regular pentagonal plate
A hexagonal plane of 30 mm side, rests on the V.P. on an edge such that the surface is inclined at 45º to the V.P. Draw its projections

A circular plane having the diameter 50 mm is resting with point A of its periphery on H.P. The surface of the plane is inclined to H.P. such that the plan of the plane becomes an ellipse with minor axis 30mm.Draw the projection of the plane when the plan of the diameter through point A is inclined at 30o to V.P.and the centre of the plane is 40mm from V.P.Find the inclination of the plane with H.P.
Classify solids with shapes of drawings

A square pyramid, side of base 35 mm and axis length 50 mm is lying on the H.P. on one of its triangular faces. Draw the projections of the pyramid when the base edge contained by the triangular face on H.P. makes an angle of 45° on the V.P. keeping apex of the pyramid towards the observer
Define Representative Fraction. With reference to Representative Fraction, classify the scales
Draw isometric drawing of the following views.
Draw the following sketches: Truncated Cylinder, Frustum of a cone and Frustum of a square pyramid.

The distance between Ahmedabad and Surat is 200 km. In a railway map it is represented by a line 5 cm long. Find it’s R.F. Draw a diagonal scale to show single km. And maximum 600 km. Indicate on it following distances. (1) 222 km (2) 569 km.
A square pyramid, side of base 30 mm and height 50 mm, is resting on HP with a side of its base. Draw the projections if the axis is inclined to 45o to HP and parallel to VP
Construct the Involute of hexagon of 25 mm sides.

A rectangular plane ABCD having 60 mm X 30 mm size is parallel to V.P., and perpendicular to H.P., and P.P. Draw the projections of the rectangle when it is 40 mm in front of V.P., and one of the smaller sides is parallel to H.P. and 20 mm above it.
Write the advantages of CAD.
